HTML extraction benchmark 2026: readability versus model-based extraction

We compared four HTML extraction strategies on five hundred pages: a readability-style density heuristic, a model-based extractor, a headless-browser text dump, and a hand-written selector set per site.

The density heuristic was the cheapest and reached 0.91 word-level F1 against a human-labelled main-content reference. The model-based extractor reached 0.94 F1 but cost roughly forty milliseconds of CPU per page. The headless dump was the worst on structured pages because navigation text survives the dump.

Boilerplate removal mattered more than sentence segmentation. Pages that keep a cookie banner or a newsletter block in the extracted text lose precision on every downstream retrieval query.

Token budget

Truncating an extracted page to ten thousand characters lost less than three percent of quotable spans, because the main content almost always sorts early in the document. Truncation at two thousand characters began to cut real evidence on long technical articles.

Reproduction

The harness, the labelled set and the per-page scores are published with the report. No proprietary model was used; the model-based row refers to an open weights extractor.
